items.quote: .claude/
items.what: .styluaignore is fully dead: its one entry, .claude/, names a hidden directory that StyLua never walks, so the file can be deleted
items.why: The gate and CI both run `stylua --check .` (StyLua 2.5.2). Tested outside the repository with the repository's stylua.toml and the same version: a badly formatted .claude/a.lua and .hid/a.lua are both skipped with no .styluaignore present, while vis/a.lua is reported; adding the ignore file changes nothing. StyLua's directory walk skips dot-prefixed paths, and a file passed by explicit path is not filtered by .styluaignore unless --respect-ignores is given, which nothing here passes. `rg --hidden styluaignore .` finds no reference in workflows, docs, AGENTS.md or the project profile. By contrast luacheck does walk hidden directories (tested the same way), so the '.claude/**' exclude in .luacheckrc is live. Medium because the file was added on purpose in the commit titled 'Standards pass: ... .claude ignore' and a future StyLua could change its hidden-path default.
items.reason: For the repository's own invocations the claim holds: in a copy of the tree with StyLua 2.5.2, `stylua --check .` reports vis/a.lua and skips .claude/x.lua with or without .styluaignore, `stylua --check .claude/x.lua` reports it both ways, and CI, AGENTS.md, README and the profile all run plain `--check .` with no hook. But the file is not inert: `stylua --check --respect-ignores .claude/x.lua` passes with it and fails without it, and `stylua --check -a .` reports the two .claude files only without it, so deletion changes behaviour for an editor format-on-save integration (these commonly pass --respect-ignores) or any --allow-hidden run on worktree copies under .claude/; only the owner can say whether one is in use.

items.what: Map.lua:12 restates the raid/dungeon split as a hand-kept instance-ID set; the canonical classification is the Map DB2 InstanceType the generator already reads (tools/gen_legacy.py:482-489, 790) but does not emit into Data/Legacy.lua entries.
items.why: gen_legacy.py validates instanceType (1 dungeon, 2 raid) against Map.InstanceType and builds completion raids from InstanceType == 2; Map.lua:444 picks the portal atlas from its own literal set instead. Checked the pinned Map-1.60.1.70009.csv: current instance entries (249 raid; 2959/2998/2999/36/389 etc. dungeons) agree today, so no live drift, but a new raid entrance (e.g. a Forever-only raid) would be drawn as a dungeon portal with no generator failure. Fix: emit instanceType (or a raid flag) on instance entries and read it here.
